seo.title: A2 vs A1 Milk: What's the Difference and Which is Better?
seo.description: Understand the critical differences between A1 and A2 milk. Learn why indigenous Indian cows (like Gir) produce A2 milk and how it affects your health and digestion.

content:
The Great Milk Debate: A1 vs A2

For decades, milk has been a staple of the Indian diet. But in recent years, a massive shift has occurred in our understanding of dairy, leading to the rise of A2 milk. But what exactly is the difference between A1 and A2 milk, and why does it matter?

The Science Behind the Proteins

Milk contains various proteins, the most prominent being Casein, which makes up about 80% of milk protein. The two most common forms of beta-casein are A1 and A2. The difference between them lies in just a single amino acid in their protein chain.

A1 Milk: The Modern Mutation

A1 milk comes from cows of Western origin (like Holstein Friesian and Jersey). Due to a genetic mutation thousands of years ago, these cows produce A1 beta-casein. When digested, A1 protein breaks down to produce a peptide called BCM-7 (Beta-casomorphin-7). Research suggests BCM-7 is linked to inflammation, digestive discomfort (often mistaken for lactose intolerance), and other health issues.

A2 Milk: The Original Superfood

A2 milk is produced by ancient, indigenous breeds of cows, such as the Indian Gir, Sahiwal, and Red Sindhi. These cows were not subjected to the genetic mutation, meaning their milk only contains A2 beta-casein. A2 milk does not produce BCM-7 upon digestion. It is easily absorbed by the human body, similar to human breast milk.

Why We Only Use A2 Milk

At Namo Narayana, we are committed to tradition and health. That's why we source our milk exclusively from free-grazing indigenous Gir cows. The resulting A2 milk is then transformed through the traditional Bilona process into our pure, golden A2 Gir Cow Ghee—ensuring you get maximum nutrition without the inflammatory risks associated with A1 dairy.
